item.title: Meta unveils Muse Spark Open, runs on Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios
item.description:
Meta unveils Muse Spark Open, runs on Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios

Meta announced the Muse Spark Open AI model today, calling it the “most capable US open-weight model to date.”

🔍 Overview

  • The company also says it’s the “first model in its class” that can “run on your desktop using two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios with the latest MLX framework.”
  • Meta and Apple, typically rivals, worked together on the launch and are publicly supporting each other.

🧩 How it works

  • The new model is a “natively multimodal model” with 816 billion total parameters.
  • It “excels at long‑horizon tasks, complex software engineering, and multi‑step reasoning.”
  • Apple’s MLX is described as an “array framework” for ML tasks on Apple Silicon and is used to run Muse Spark Open on the Mac Studios.

⚙️ Key details

  • Model name: Muse Spark Open
  • Weight release: Today (weights releasing today)
  • Hardware requirement: Two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios
  • Software framework: MLX (Apple’s array framework for ML on Apple Silicon)
  • Capabilities: Multimodal processing, long‑horizon reasoning, software‑engineering assistance, multi‑step reasoning

🚀 Availability

  • “Muse Spark Open – weights releasing today – runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work with @johnternus and Apple,” Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said on X.
  • “Congrats to the team!” new Apple CEO John Ternus replied.

💡 Why it matters

  • Meta chief AI officer Alexandr Wang told Axios that the companies have been collaborating for several months, noting the partnership as a sign of “mommy and daddy playing nice again.”
  • Apple published a technical post about MLX, highlighting its role in enabling Muse Spark Open and two other open models on Apple Silicon.

item.title: Epic Games adopts AI‑first approach for Disney shooter, delaying release
item.description:
Epic Games adopts AI‑first approach for Disney shooter, delaying release

Epic Games announced that its unannounced Disney shooter will be built under an “AI‑first” mandate, pushing developers to use AI tools such as Anthropic’s Claude for both code and art. The project has been moved out of its original March release window.

🔍 Overview

  • Project: an unannounced shooter featuring characters from Marvel and Star Wars.
  • Collaboration: part of a multiyear partnership between Epic Games and Disney, which invested $1.5 billion in Epic in 2024.
  • Shift: developers have been given an “AI‑first” mandate to use tools like Anthropic’s Claude.

⚙️ AI‑first mandate

  • Developers were told to use AI tools such as Anthropic’s Claude.
  • One of the game’s directors said to staff, “No more hand‑written code.”
  • Staff were also told that all of the game’s art will be “generated with full AI workflows.”
  • Epic spokesperson Jake Jones said the company is “embracing AI‑accelerated development.”

📅 Timeline & status

  • Original target: March release window.
  • Current status: delayed beyond the March window (no new date provided).

💡 Why it matters

  • Shows large‑scale use of generative AI for both programming and visual content in a AAA title.
  • Epic already uses AI in Fortnite, which has previously featured Disney characters like an AI Darth Vader.
  • AI game‑development tools are also emerging from other large companies, such as Meta and Google.
  • Epic CEO Tim Sweeney has pushed for Steam to drop its “made with AI” tag, arguing that “AI will be involved in nearly all future production.”
  • Earlier this year, Epic laid off over 1,000 employees following a downturn in Fortnite engagement since 2025.

🛠️ Tools & workflow

AI Tool Intended Use
Anthropic’s Claude Generate code and create art assets
